title: FCT-GAN: Enhancing Table Synthesis via Fourier Transform
summary: Argues that tabular GANs miss correlations spanning the whole row and are sensitive to the order in which columns are presented, and proposes FCT-GAN, which tokenizes each encoded row with a CNN filter and then passes the tokens through Fourier network blocks in both generator and discriminator so that learnable weights over all frequencies capture global column relations. The paper first demonstrates the permutation problem empirically across three column orders, then reports the smallest variation for its own model. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the five synthesizers it benchmarks throughout, and the conditional vector FCT-GAN adopts is the one the paper attributes to CTGAN and describes as later improved by CTAB-GAN+, together with the variational Gaussian mixture encoding of continuous columns.
evidence: section II states that CT-GAN and CTAB-GAN improve synthesis through preprocessing steps and that the conditional vector was designed by CT-GAN and later improved by CTAB-GAN, reducing mode collapse on minority categories; section IV.B.2 adopts that conditional vector and the variational Gaussian mixture encoder for continuous columns from CTAB-GAN+; Tables I, III and IV report CT-GAN and TVAE among the five baselines across seven datasets and three column orders; Table V records that CT-GAN and TVAE could not be trained on the Youth dataset because of conditional vector dimensionality

title: RCC-GAN: Regularized Compound Conditional GAN for Large-Scale Tabular Data Synthesis
summary: Replaces the per-column mask conditional vector of prior tabular GANs with a compound conditional vector that carries several columns at once, adds a regularization term over the fitted mixture parameters, and redesigns the continuous-column transformer so multivariate distributions survive encoding, targeting tables too wide for one-hot conditioning to remain tractable. CTGAN is the design the paper works from and against: it reproduces CTGAN's conditional vector definition in full before proposing its own, follows CTGAN in mapping discrete and binary columns through a tanh transformer, builds its continuous-column encoder on the same variational Gaussian mixture idea, takes the Gumbel softmax in its residual blocks from the CTGAN authors, and reports CTGAN as one of the GAN baselines it is measured against.
evidence: section III restates the CTGAN conditional vector as equation 10 and states that conditioning the generator on it significantly improves generalizability and stability; section IV notes that following CTGAN the paper also uses the tanh mapping for discrete and binary columns while designing a new VGM-based transformer for continuous ones; the residual-network section credits Xu et al. for the Gumbel softmax it adopts; the results tables report CTGAN alongside MotGAN, VeeGAN, ItsGAN, InvGAN and BctGAN as baselines

title: Comparing the Utility and Disclosure Risk of Synthetic Data with Samples of Microdata
summary: Puts synthetic data and conventional sampled microdata on the same risk-utility map, so that a data custodian can ask whether releasing a synthetic file is better or worse than releasing a sample, and applies the framework to four census microdata sets. CTGAN is one of the three synthesisers whose output is measured, pinned at version 0.4.3 and run five times per dataset under different random seeds; the paper also credits its mode-specific normalization for handling non-Gaussian and multimodal columns and varies the differential-privacy parameter across its runs.
evidence: the introduction states the experiments used four census microdata sets with synthetic data generated by three state-of-the-art methods, CTGAN, Synthpop and DataSynthesizer; section 2.2 credits CTGAN by Xu et al. with mode-specific normalisation to overcome non-Gaussian and multimodal distributions; section 3.1 records that version 0.4.3 of CTGAN was used for all experiments and that five models were created per dataset under different random seeds

title: REaLTabFormer: Generating Realistic Relational and Tabular Data using Transformers
summary: Generates relational datasets with transformers rather than statistical models: a GPT-style model learns the parent table, and a sequence-to-sequence model conditioned on the frozen parent encoding produces the child rows, with an overfitting criterion based on a statistical bootstrap deciding when to stop training. SDV is the relational baseline the result is measured against — the paper identifies the Hierarchical Modeling Algorithm of Patki et al., which fits Gaussian copulas within and across tables, as the existing approach for relational synthesis, and its figures plot SDV's output beside REaLTabFormer's on the parent-child joint distributions and on a daily sales series.
evidence: the related-work section states that models able to produce relational datasets are limited, citing Patki et al., and that existing models are based on Hierarchical Modeling Algorithms in which Gaussian copulas learn the joint distributions for each and across tables; Figure 2 plots the daily mean of the Rossmann sales variable for the original data, REaLTabFormer and SDV, and Figure 3 compares the parent-child joint distributions of the original data, SDV and REaLTabFormer

title: Membership Inference Attacks against Synthetic Data through Overfitting Detection
summary: Reframes membership inference against synthetic data as overfitting detection: DOMIAS scores a target record by the ratio of its density under the synthetic distribution to its density under a reference population, so that records the generator has locally overfitted are identified without assuming the attacker knows the training procedure. TVAE, released with CTGAN, is the generator the attack is developed and calibrated against — training-set size and epoch count are swept on TVAE to control how much it overfits, the private heart-failure experiment generates from TVAE, and CTGAN and TVAE both appear in the wider comparison of generators by privacy-utility trade-off.
evidence: section 5.1 states the California Housing experiments use TVAE to generate synthetic data and vary the number of TVAE training samples and training epochs; the medical experiment generates synthetic data from TVAE on a private heart-failure dataset of about 40,000 records; the generator comparison evaluates GAN, WGAN-GP, CTGAN and TVAE, NFlow, PATE-GAN, PrivBayes and ADS-GAN, reporting CTGAN on the unfavourable side of the additive-noise curve
